domains.name: Screening and Evaluation of Employees, Physicians, Vendors, and Other Agents
Communication, Education, and Training on Compliance Issues
Privacy Monitoring, Auditing, and Internal Reporting Systems

domain_guidance.summary: This domain focuses on the development and implementation of privacy standards, policies, and procedures within a healthcare organization to ensure that all regulatory requirements are met consistently across the entire facility for patient data.

This domain focuses on the oversight and management of privacy compliance programs to ensure organizational integrity and adherence to legal mandates while maintaining the standards of patient data protection and security across the enterprise.

This domain addresses the processes for screening and evaluating employees, physicians, vendors, and other agents to ensure they meet the necessary privacy standards and do not pose a risk to the organization or patient data.

This domain involves the communication, education, and training strategies required to address compliance issues, ensuring that all staff members understand their roles and responsibilities regarding the protection of sensitive patient health information in daily operations.

This domain covers the systems and processes for monitoring, auditing, and internal reporting of privacy compliance to identify potential vulnerabilities and ensure that all organizational privacy policies are being followed by staff at all levels.

This domain focuses on the establishment and enforcement of clear disciplinary actions for instances of non-compliance, ensuring that all staff understand the consequences of failing to adhere to established privacy policies and procedures within the organization.

This domain covers the formal procedures for conducting investigations and implementing necessary remedial measures following identified compliance breaches to prevent future occurrences and maintain the trust of patients and regulatory bodies alike in the organization.

editorial.overview: The Certified in Healthcare Privacy Compliance (CHPC) designation is offered by the Health Care Compliance Association (HCCA). This professional certification validates knowledge of healthcare privacy regulations, industry standards, and operational practices. It covers seven distinct domains, including privacy program oversight, employee screening, communication, monitoring, and investigations, ensuring that certified professionals can manage and maintain privacy compliance programs within complex healthcare organizations. This credential demonstrates a commitment to maintaining the highest standards of patient data protection.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Candidates should focus on their professional compliance experience to prepare for the assessment. Review the official Health Care Compliance Association (HCCA) exam guide to identify specific subject areas for testing. Attend healthcare compliance events, engage with industry experts, and participate in the HCCA net social network to discuss regulations. Use the official exam guide to familiarize yourself with the testing environment before your scheduled appointment.
editorial.who_should_take: This certification is intended for professionals currently working in healthcare compliance, privacy, or legal roles. Candidates should possess practical experience in managing privacy programs, addressing regulatory obligations, and overseeing internal reporting systems to safeguard sensitive patient information effectively.
